verdicts.title: Stop-at-epsilon still only fires at log boundaries for Monte-Carlo accountant modes
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified in the current tree. _dp_trainer.py:1171-1176 gates predict_stop_step on 'a.sampling_mode not in ("b_min_sep", "balls_in_bins")', so ctx.stop_at_step stays None for those modes; grep shows the only other writer of state.privacy_target_epsilon_reached / should_training_stop for stop-at-eps is the fallback at :3969-3977, which sits inside 'if ctrl.should_log:' (:3955). git log -S confirms the exclusion was introduced by the fix commit b7073f37 itself (PR #526, closes #392), whose body promised a per-step guard without mentioning the carve-out. _training_arguments.py:171-179 confirms b_min_sep/balls_in_bins are the auto samplers for mf_band/mf_blt/mf_bisr/mf_bsr/mf_lambda_cgd, and _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS pins balls_in_bins as the ONLY legal sampler for blt/bisr/bsr/lambda_cgd, so those four mechanisms can never get the per-step stop. Severity reduced from medium to low: (a) the carve-out is deliberate and justified in-code (Monte-Carlo PLDs are non-monotone in k and thread-count-sensitive, so the binary search is unsound there); (b) the current user documentation still describes exactly this log-boundary contract (see finding 39), so users of these modes are not misled about it; (c) the hard total_steps ceiling bounds any overrun and BallsInBins prefix accounting rounds up to epoch boundaries (atomic_unit = num_bins), so the accounted epsilon at any log boundary is already the epoch-rounded upper bound. It is a real gap in the stop-at-eps guarantee, not a mis-stated epsilon. Not a duplicate of a tsv-open issue: #688 mentions the exclusion only in passing as intentional ('MC paths are already excluded from predicted stop-at-epsilon') and its work items cover KOutOfT and BISR/lambda-CGD prefixes, not this.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_blt' (or mf_bisr/mf_bsr/mf_lambda_cgd, whose only allowed sampler is balls_in_bins; or mf_band with b_min_sep), a fixed privacy_noise_multiplier and a privacy_target_epsilon, ctx.stop_at_step is never computed. The only stop-at-eps owner is the fallback inside 'if ctrl.should_log:', so training keeps taking accounted steps after the accountant's epsilon crosses the target until the next logging boundary (up to logging_steps-1 extra accounted updates with the default logging_steps=500), and with logging_strategy='no' / logging_steps=0 the stop never fires at all and the run consumes the full calibrated horizon. Accounted epsilon is still reported truthfully; what is violated is the user's declared stopping budget, and only for the modes the current docs already describe as log-boundary-gated.

verdicts.title: predict_stop_step halts k_out_of_t runs after one accounted step (flat prefix epsilon)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. _k_out_of_t.py:28-33 documents and :92-107 implements the snap: for n_steps < self.n_steps and total_participations > 1, pld_at delegates to pld_at(self.n_steps). Numerically (uv run): with acc.cached(acc.per_step(k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.0), total_participations=4, n_steps=100))), (sp*K).epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.4083134058043343 for K in {1,2,5,50,100}; calling the real predict_stop_step on that process returns 1 for targets 0.5, 2.0 and 2.4083134058043343, and None for 3.0. Control: total_participations=1 gives a strictly increasing prefix (0.1999, 0.2451, 0.5366, 0.6233 for K=1,2,50,100) and predict_stop_step returns 37, so the pathology is confined to total_participations > 1. The trainer reaches this process via _dp_trainer.py:4282-4302 (sampling_mode='k_out_of_t' with sampling_kwargs['total_participations']), and k_out_of_t is not in the predict_stop_step exclusion list, so the boundary guard (lo == 1, no lo-1 probe) accepts the constant sequence. Stopping early is conservative for privacy, so affects_epsilon is correctly false; the harm is purely utility (an untrained model returned as a success). Severity stays low. This substantially duplicates tracked issue #688, whose work item 1 states verbatim that KOutOfT prefixes 'snap to the full-horizon bound ... too pessimistic for DPTrainer.predict_stop_step: binary search can predict the privacy target at step 1' with acceptance criterion 'KOutOfT(k > 1) does not trigger stop-at-epsilon before the configured horizon'.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: sampling_mode='k_out_of_t' with sampling_kwargs={'total_participations': k>1}, a fixed privacy_noise_multiplier and any privacy_target_epsilon at or below the full-horizon epsilon: KOutOfT.pld_at returns the full-horizon PLD for every prefix, so epsilon(K) is constant, predict_stop_step's binary search returns k0+1, and train() breaks after a single optimizer step with state.privacy_target_epsilon_reached=True and an essentially untrained model. Conservative for privacy, silent for utility apart from the 'will stop after step 1 of N' info log. Already tracked as issue #688 work item 1.

verdicts.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO Eq.(2) weight-alignment term that TRL and the paper apply
verdicts.reasoning: Verified against the primary source, not just TRL. I extracted the WPO paper PDF (arXiv:2406.11827): Section 3.2 defines the unnumbered length-normalized weight w(x,y) = exp((1/|y|) sum_t log pi(y_t|x,y<t)); Section 3.3 'Weight Alignment' then defines greedy alignment and 'sampled alignment', and it is the SAMPLED-alignment form, w(x,y) = exp((1/|y|) sum_t log [pi(y_t|x,y<t) / sum_{v in V} pi(v|x,y<t)^2]), that carries the equation number (2), followed by 'We use sampled alignment as the default alignment method in WPO'. Algorithm 1 says 'Calculate the alignment weight via Eq. (2)'. So Eq. (2) is the aligned weight and opaque implements only the Section-3.2 precursor. _wpo.py:33-46 returns (masked logp sum / count).detach().exp() with no logits and no alignment term; the trainer path is no better: _dpo_trainer.py:1251-1267 (_wpo_weight) builds per-token logps from logits and just forwards them to wpo_weights, and :1138-1144 multiplies the loss by chosen*rejected. Installed trl 1.12.0 dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606 computes lse1/lse2 and log_denom = lse2 - 2*lse1 = log(sum_v p_v^2) under the comment 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper'. The divergence is not proportional (log sum_v p_v^2 varies with per-token confidence), so cross-example relative weighting differs. packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518 pins it with a strict xfail; the module docstring (_wpo.py:3-22) and docs/alignment/trainers.md:281-284 present the shipped weighting as arXiv:2406.11827 without caveat. Utility only (the weight is detached and per-example), so affects_epsilon false is correct. Not a duplicate: the two tsv-open umbrellas the reporter names, #323 and #475, are both actually closed on GitHub (2026-08-27) and neither body mentions WPO or use_weighting; #475 is about DP/sensitivity assumptions of DPO losses, not paper fidelity.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets DPOConfig(use_weighting=True) — advertised in docs/alignment/trainers.md as WPO (arXiv:2406.11827) and in _wpo.py's docstring as the paper's weighting. Opaque applies exp(mean masked log p_t), i.e. the paper's Section-3.2 precursor weight, while both the paper's default (Eq. (2), sampled alignment) and TRL's use_weighting apply exp(mean [log p_t - log sum_v p_v^2]). Per-example weights, and hence the relative weighting across the batch and the resulting training dynamics, differ systematically from TRL and from the cited method, with no user-facing caveat; only a strict xfail in the internal parity suite records the gap. No privacy impact.

verdicts.title: Stop-at-epsilon user guide still documents the pre-#392 log-boundary-only behavior
verdicts.reasoning: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:69-81 still reads 'training halts at the first logging boundary where the accumulated ε ... meets or exceeds the target' and 'The check runs every logging_steps (so setting logging_steps=0 disables it silently)'. Since b7073f37 that is false for every deterministic accountant: the stop is a per-step integer comparison against ctx.stop_at_step (_dp_trainer.py:1178-1193 sets it, :1874-1881 acts on it), and packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_dp_trainer.py:256 (test_stop_at_epsilon_independent_of_logging_cadence) asserts logging_steps=1 and logging_steps=999 stop at the same step. The in-source comment at _training_arguments.py:478-481 ('training halts at the first log boundary where ε ≥ target_epsilon') repeats the stale claim. git show --stat b7073f37 confirms the commit touched only _dp_trainer.py and its tests — no docs. The doc remains accurate only for b_min_sep/balls_in_bins (finding 36) and for the fallback case where the monotone-boundary guard rejects the prediction. Low severity, docs-only; not covered concretely by the tsv-open docs umbrella #324.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reads the Stop-at-ε section and believes stop-at-ε is gated on logging cadence — e.g. sets logging_steps=0/logging_strategy='no' expecting the target not to be enforced while leaving privacy_target_epsilon set. On any deterministic accountant (poisson, random_allocation, k_out_of_t, cyclic_poisson, sequential, mf_identity) the run now stops at the binary-searched step regardless of logging. Conversely a b_min_sep / balls_in_bins user gets no hint that their mode is the one still on the weaker log-boundary contract.

verdicts.title: from_hf doc still claims adamw_torch_fused maps to optim_args={'fused': True}
verdicts.reasoning: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:283 still lists 'adamw_torch_fused → adamw + optim_args={"fused": True}'. The code does not do that: _hf_convert.py:254-262 emits a RuntimeWarning and returns {'optim': 'adamw'} with no optim_args (comment explicitly notes forwarding fused=True used to raise TypeError at optimizer-build time, #389), and _optim.py:87 maps the alias to ('adamw', {}). test_compat_hf.py:238-249 pins the behavior including 'assert not opaque.optim_args'. grep shows line 283 is the only mention of adamw_torch_fused in that doc, so nothing else corrects it. Docs-only, low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user following the conversion table expects (or hand-writes) optim_args={'fused': True} alongside optim='adamw'; the converter never produces it and the opaque functional AdamW factory has no fused argument, so a hand-written value is rejected at optimizer build. At minimum the user mis-reports what their converted run executes and does not learn that the fused-kernel request is dropped with a RuntimeWarning.

verdicts.title: docs/alignment/trainers.md still omits the supported chunked_nll SFT loss (OPQ-142 residual)
verdicts.reasoning: docs/alignment/trainers.md:109-110 reads '`loss_type` selects the per-example head: `"nll"` (standard cross-entropy) or `"dft"` (Dynamic Fine-Tuning)', and line 62 likewise comments 'loss_type="nll", # or "dft"'. chunked_nll is a fully supported third value: _sft_config.py:77-80 documents it on the field, _sft_trainer.py dispatches it (:185, :231-235, :533), and test_compat_trl_sft.py:78-84 pins the config carry-through. docs/reference/transformers.md:472 (and :449) already lists all three, so the two pages contradict each other. grep -rn 'chunked' docs/ returns only reference/transformers.md and model-patches.md — nothing under docs/alignment. af29e4a9 ('docs(transformers): align reference tables with dataclass defaults', #477) touched only docs/reference/transformers.md, confirming the second site was left behind. Docs-only omission, low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user working from the SFT/DPO trainers guide sees only 'nll' and 'dft' as loss_type values and never learns the memory-saving fused, logits-free chunked_nll path exists, even though SFTConfig accepts it and the API reference lists it; the two doc pages state different supported value sets.
